applicationInfo.name: Threat Model Export
applicationInfo.description: Public, Apache-2.0 sample repository (sample-agentic-code-review-gate) built for a security-conference demo. It shows an AI code reviewer designed as a fail-closed security control: a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/agentic-review.yml) runs two independent Claude model calls (discovery, then falsification/validation) against every same-repo pull request, using Amazon Bedrock via GitHub OIDC (secret AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN) or the Anthropic API (secret ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Rules (RULES.yaml) and prompts (.github/review-prompts/*.md) are read from the PR BASE commit; the agent is code-only (Read/Grep/Glob) with a prefetched diff; a CI step parses SHA-scoped markers ([REVIEWED]/[BLOCK-MERGE]) and posts one PR comment; every abnormal path fails closed. The review target is a tiny Python asset service (app/files.py path containment, app/tokens.py constant-time token check with redacted logging) that is deliberately attacked by four demo PRs (guard removal, prompt injection, rules disarming, CI credential exfiltration). The README also describes a deliberately insecure naive lane and demo tooling that are not present in this checkout. Business value: reputational (a security sample must not itself be exploitable) and educational; the assets that matter are the integrity of the merge gate, the cloud/API credentials the workflow holds, and the cost of model invocations.

assumptions.content: The repository is public and Apache-2.0 licensed; the source code and the PR diffs have no confidentiality requirement. Confidentiality concerns are limited to the workflow credentials.

The system under analysis is the AI review gate (agentic-review.yml, review prompts, RULES.yaml, ci.yml). The Python app under app/ is the demo review target and is not deployed as a service anywhere.
Files referenced by the README but absent from this checkout (naive-review.yml, demo/, tests/, talk/) are out of scope. In particular the deliberately insecure naive lane is not analysed.

The workflow runs on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners and calls Amazon Bedrock in vars.AWS_REGION (default us-west-2) through an IAM role assumed via GitHub OIDC. The Anthropic API path is a fallback the maintainer may configure instead.
Branch protection (or a ruleset) on main requires the 'Agentic AI Review' and 'Unit tests' status checks, requires a PR, and has admin bypass disabled. Without this, the gate is advisory.
The IAM role for AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN trusts only this repository's OIDC subject (repo:<owner>/<repo>:pull_request or narrower) and grants only bedrock:InvokeModel* on the inference profiles used.
The primary adversary is a same-repository contributor with write access (or an attacker holding such an account), because only same-repo PRs run the workflow with secrets.

The financial impact of a compromise is bounded by model invocation cost within the Bedrock role's permissions plus reputational damage to a security sample; no customer data or revenue-bearing system is involved.

The IAM role trust policy for AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN sets both token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud = sts.amazonaws.com and a token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub condition scoped to this repository (e.g. repo:<owner>/<repo>:pull_request), per AWS guidance that an unscoped sub lets any GitHub organization or repository assume the role. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-idp_oidc.html

The role's permission policy grants only bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream on the specific inference-profile and foundation-model ARNs used (default profiles us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 and us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8), following AWS's least-privilege examples for Bedrock model access. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/simplified-amazon-bedrock-model-access/

anthropics/claude-code-action, in prompt-driven mode with --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob, does not expose any tool that performs network egress or GitHub API writes to the model, and does not inject PR title/body into the model context. The github_token input is used only by the action's own plumbing.

Nation-state, competitor, terrorist and cyber-mercenary actors are not relevant: the repository is a public demo with no proprietary data, no customers and no infrastructure beyond a model-invocation role.

Anyone able to open a same-repository pull request is treated as fully adversarial, regardless of employment relationship, because GitHub account compromise is common and the workflow cannot distinguish a compromised account from a malicious one.

GitHub masks registered secret values and the AWS credentials exported by configure-aws-credentials in step logs, but masking is exact-string based: values that are transformed (base64, split, reversed) or quoted by the model in a different form are not masked. The workflow's own perl redaction is therefore treated as the effective control for model output.
AWS STS session credentials issued to the role remain valid until their expiry (default 1 hour) even after the GitHub job finishes; the repository does not use a shorter role-duration-seconds.

SHA-scoped markers cannot be pre-planted in PR content: the head SHA depends on the content, so an author cannot commit a file containing '[REVIEWED] <head sha>' for that same commit. Marker forgery therefore requires steering the model (T001) or changing the workflow (T003), and replaying an earlier run's output is impossible.

Claude Code's --allowedTools 'Read,Grep,Glob' in non-interactive mode denies every other tool (Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch, MCP tools) rather than merely skipping approval prompts; the README reports the denial as visible in transcripts.

The maintainer will apply the GitHub-side mitigations (CODEOWNERS on .github/** and RULES.yaml, rulesets without bypass, required check names) before relying on the gate for anything beyond the demo; these cannot be expressed in the repository's files and are therefore tracked as identified, not resolved.

anthropics/claude-code-action at the pinned SHA accepts a Claude Code settings/permissions input (or honours a checked-in .claude/settings.json) that can deny Read on specific paths; if it does not, the equivalent constraint requires running the agent in a container job with a minimal filesystem.

Risk acceptance criteria used in Phase 8: a threat is Accepted only where the README explicitly names the trade-off (cost of two model calls, nondeterministic verdicts, fail-closed outages) or where the impact is bounded to public code or human confusion without affecting the check run. Everything that could turn the gate green on attacker terms, or expose credentials, stays Open until the owner acts.
The residual-risk decisions recorded here are the analyst's proposals; the repository owner has not yet reviewed or approved them.

mitigations.content: IMPLEMENTED: Review contract (RULES.yaml, discovery.md, validate.md) is loaded from the pull request BASE commit, never from the PR head; a missing or empty prompt fails the job.
IMPLEMENTED: Code-only agent tool allow-list (Read, Grep, Glob) with a 40-turn cap in both passes; the agent has no execution or network tool.
IMPLEMENTED: The diff is prefetched as a data file outside the checkout and the invocation prompt contains no PR title, body or comments; the agent never runs git or gh.

IMPLEMENTED: Two independent model invocations (discovery then falsification) with prompts that treat in-diff text and the candidate list as untrusted, require code-grounded evidence, and limit BLOCKING to a closed list.

IMPLEMENTED: Deterministic fail-closed gate on SHA-scoped markers; every abnormal path (errored step, empty output, missing marker, oversized candidates) exits 1, and a CI step, not the model, posts the single PR comment.
IMPLEMENTED: Credential hygiene: checkout token not persisted, minimal job permissions, cloud credentials assumed last and only when Bedrock is configured.

IMPLEMENTED (partial): Regex redaction of AWS key ids, ARNs, 12-digit account ids and labelled secret values in model output before it is logged or posted, on top of GitHub's exact-string secret masking.
IMPLEMENTED: Fork guard on every step plus a distinct job name for fork PRs, relying on GitHub withholding secrets from fork-triggered pull_request events.
IMPLEMENTED: All third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs with version comments; Python test dependencies version-pinned.
IMPLEMENTED: Scratch paths are removed before being recreated and the diff lives under $RUNNER_TEMP, so PR-committed files or symlinks at those paths cannot redirect writes or pre-seed gate inputs.
IMPLEMENTED: Blocking rule 'rules-may-only-tighten' makes any weakening of RULES.yaml, the prompts or the workflow a BLOCKING finding when reviewed against the base contract.
IMPLEMENTED (partial): Per-PR concurrency cancellation, 30-minute job timeout, 40-turn cap per pass and a candidate-size cap bound the cost of a single PR's review.
IMPLEMENTED: Demo app guards: resolved-path containment (follows symlinks), absolute/empty path rejection, constant-time token comparison and prefix-only token logging.
IMPLEMENTED: Blocking rules no-guard-removal and no-secret-logging give the reviewer an explicit checklist for the two app guards, including the specific weak replacements attackers use.
IMPLEMENTED: The unit-test job that executes PR code runs with a read-only token, no repository secrets and a non-persisted checkout credential.
Protect .github/** and RULES.yaml with CODEOWNERS plus a branch ruleset that requires code-owner review and forbids bypass, so a PR cannot merge a modified reviewer without a second human.

Move the privileged review job to a default-branch-defined workflow_run lane that consumes the PR diff as an artifact, so the code that reviews a PR can never be edited by that PR (and fork PRs can be reviewed safely).
Verify branch protection/rulesets on main: required checks match the current job names exactly, no admin bypass, PR required; pin the check name in the workflow-invariants test.

Harden the Bedrock IAM role: repository-scoped OIDC subject and audience conditions, InvokeModel-only permissions on the exact inference-profile/foundation-model ARNs, and the shortest practical session duration.

Add cost and misuse monitoring: Bedrock budget and invocation alarms, model invocation logging with restricted access, CloudTrail alerting on role assumption, GitHub Actions spending limit, and trigger filters that skip draft or docs-only PRs.

Constrain what the agent's Read tool can reach: deny-list /proc, home, temp and .git paths via Claude Code permission settings, drop the unused ANTHROPIC_API_KEY input when Bedrock is active, and consider a container job with a minimal filesystem.

Treat secret-shaped content in model output as a gate failure rather than something to redact: broaden the patterns (raw AWS secret keys, GitHub and Anthropic token prefixes, JWTs, long base64 blobs) and withhold the output entirely when they match.
Add an upper bound on reviewable diff size and reject Trojan-Source characters, so an attacker cannot exhaust the agents' turns or context to hide a small change.
Close the run-time install gap: pin the Claude Code CLI version, hash-pin Python test dependencies, and review action updates through Dependabot before adopting new SHAs.
Preserve an audit trail independent of editable PR comments: upload the redacted outputs and execution transcript as workflow artifacts and reference run id and SHA in the comment.
Measure the reviewer empirically against the attack corpus after every model, prompt or action change, and pin model ids so behaviour changes are deliberate.
Make the bot comment unambiguous and non-authoritative: include run id and SHA in the marker, keep lane markers distinct, and document that the check run, not the comment, is the verdict.
Scope the secret-derived USE_BEDROCK expression to the job (or a single step) instead of the workflow-level env block (ASH finding 1).
When reusing the pattern on non-public code, keep model calls on Bedrock with restricted invocation logging (or zero retention) and review the Anthropic API fallback's data terms.
Define the recovery path for outages and false blocks: bounded retries, documented re-run, and a code-owner override procedure that never weakens the required check.

businessContext.description: Public, Apache-2.0 sample repository (sample-agentic-code-review-gate) built for a security-conference demo. It shows an AI code reviewer designed as a fail-closed security control: a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/agentic-review.yml) runs two independent Claude model calls (discovery, then falsification/validation) against every same-repo pull request, using Amazon Bedrock via GitHub OIDC (secret AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN) or the Anthropic API (secret ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Rules (RULES.yaml) and prompts (.github/review-prompts/*.md) are read from the PR BASE commit; the agent is code-only (Read/Grep/Glob) with a prefetched diff; a CI step parses SHA-scoped markers ([REVIEWED]/[BLOCK-MERGE]) and posts one PR comment; every abnormal path fails closed. The review target is a tiny Python asset service (app/files.py path containment, app/tokens.py constant-time token check with redacted logging) that is deliberately attacked by four demo PRs (guard removal, prompt injection, rules disarming, CI credential exfiltration). The README also describes a deliberately insecure naive lane and demo tooling that are not present in this checkout. Business value: reputational (a security sample must not itself be exploitable) and educational; the assets that matter are the integrity of the merge gate, the cloud/API credentials the workflow holds, and the cost of model invocations.

components.description: Ephemeral VM that runs every step of the review job. Holds GITHUB_TOKEN, and after the credentials step the AWS session credentials, in process environment. All steps carry the fork guard head.repo.full_name == github.repository.

components.name: Contract and diff preparation steps (actions/checkout, extract base-ref rules and prompts, prefetch diff)

components.name: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials (OIDC to STS)
components.description: CONTROL 3: runs only when USE_BEDROCK == 'true'; exchanges the GitHub OIDC token for short-lived STS credentials for secrets.AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN in vars.AWS_REGION (default us-west-2) and exports them into the job environment for the remaining steps.

components.name: Discovery agent (anthropics/claude-code-action pass 1)
components.description: CONTROL 2 part 2 / CONTROL 4 stage 1: reads .review-prompts/discovery.md, the prefetched diff and any repository file via Read/Grep/Glob, and emits a candidate list ending in [DISCOVERY] <head sha>. Receives github_token and anthropic_api_key inputs and inherits AWS session credentials from the environment. Installs the Claude Code CLI at run time.

components.name: Validation agent (anthropics/claude-code-action pass 2)
components.description: CONTROL 4 stage 2: independent invocation that reads .review-prompts/validate.md, the diff, the repository and .review-candidates.md (treated as untrusted evidence), falsifies candidates, classifies survivors against the closed BLOCKING list, and emits [REVIEWED] <sha> plus optionally [BLOCK-MERGE] <sha>. Only this pass's output reaches the PR.

components.name: Capture, redact, comment and gate steps (CI shell)
components.description: CONTROL 5: extracts the last result from each pass's execution_file with jq; perl-redacts AKIA/ASIA key ids, arn:aws*, 12-digit account ids and labelled secret values; fails closed if [DISCOVERY] marker is missing or candidates exceed 120000 bytes; posts or updates ONE PR comment keyed by <!-- agentic-ai-review --> (filtered to github-actions[bot] author) using GITHUB_TOKEN; final gate exits 1 unless validate.outcome == success, review-output.md non-empty, [REVIEWED] <sha> present and [BLOCK-MERGE] <sha> absent.

threatActors.name: Hacktivist

threatActors.description: Inexperienced attacker using public tooling: opens noisy fork PRs, copies known prompt-injection payloads into a PR (only effective with write access), or runs secret scanners over public logs (covered in more depth by TA015).

threatActors.name: Privileged User
threatActors.description: The repository maintainer/admin making mistakes rather than acting maliciously: leaving admin bypass on branch protection enabled, not requiring the 'Agentic AI Review' check, configuring an OIDC trust policy without a repository-scoped sub condition, granting the Bedrock role broader permissions than InvokeModel, or storing a long-lived ANTHROPIC_API_KEY instead of using OIDC.

threatActors.description: Vendors whose code or service the gate depends on: GitHub (runner, secrets, OIDC), Anthropic (claude-code-action, Claude Code CLI, model behaviour and API), AWS (STS, Bedrock), PyPI package maintainers. Risk is both compromise (see TA014) and benign change: an action update that starts injecting PR context, a model update that changes marker compliance.

threatActors.name: Terrorist Organization
threatActors.description: A group with limited offensive cyber capability, primarily using the internet for propaganda and recruitment

threatActors.type: Private Sector Offensive Actor / Cyber Mercenary
threatActors.name: Private Sector Offensive Actor
threatActors.description: A commercial vendor developing zero-day exploits and spyware for client-selected targets

threatActors.name: Malicious or compromised same-repository contributor
threatActors.description: A GitHub identity with write access to the repository (a real contributor, a contributor whose account or token was phished, or a maintainer's compromised laptop). Only this actor can open pull requests that run agentic-review.yml with repository secrets and GITHUB_TOKEN. Techniques modelled by the README's attack PRs: smuggling a guard removal inside a polished feature (attack 1), prompt injection in code comments and PR body (attack 2), disarming RULES.yaml/prompts/workflow (attack 3), and exfiltrating CI secrets from a test hook (attack 4). Also able to spam pushes to drive model cost, and to edit the workflow file itself.

threatActors.name: Software supply-chain attacker (third-party action, Claude Code CLI, Python packages)
threatActors.description: Compromises something the job executes rather than the repository: a new commit of anthropics/claude-code-action or aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials (mitigated by SHA pinning), the Claude Code CLI package the action downloads at run time (not pinned by this repo), the pytest/PyYAML wheels ci.yml installs (version-pinned but not hash-pinned), or the setup-python toolchain. Payload runs with GITHUB_TOKEN and, inside the agent steps, with the AWS session credentials. Historical precedent: tj-actions/changed-files (2025), ultralytics PyPI (2024).

threatActors.name: Automated secret harvester scanning public GitHub artifacts
threatActors.description: Bots that continuously scrape public repositories, Actions logs and PR comments for credential shapes (AWS keys, API keys, tokens) and immediately abuse them, typically for LLM API resale or crypto-mining. Relevant because this workflow prints redacted model output to public logs and posts it to public PR comments; anything the regex redaction misses is harvested within minutes.

trustZones.name: Pull request author (untrusted input origin)
trustZones.description: Everything a PR author controls: file contents, filenames, symlinks, commit messages, PR title/body, and for same-repo PRs the workflow file the run will execute. Authenticated identity, but content is assumed hostile (A013).

trustZones.name: GitHub SaaS platform (repository, PRs, Actions control plane, secrets, logs)
trustZones.description: GitHub-operated services the repository relies on: git storage for main and PR branches, PR conversations and check runs, the Actions scheduler/secrets injector/OIDC issuer, and run logs. Trusted for platform integrity (secret masking, fork isolation) but the data it holds mixes trusted base-commit content with untrusted PR-head content, and logs/comments are world-readable.

trustZones.name: Review job runner: deterministic CI steps
trustZones.description: The ubuntu-latest VM and the shell/action steps defined in agentic-review.yml: checkout, contract extraction, diff prefetch, credential assumption, capture/redact, comment posting and the gate. These steps hold GITHUB_TOKEN and AWS session credentials. Trust is only Medium because, for same-repo pull_request events, the workflow definition itself comes from the PR merge ref: without branch protection/CODEOWNERS on .github/**, the PR author can rewrite these steps (README 'What this does not solve').

trustZones.name: AI reviewer agent sandbox (LLM-driven processes)
trustZones.description: The two claude-code-action invocations. Same VM and same environment as the CI steps, but behaviour is steered by attacker-controllable text (diff, file contents, candidate list). Confined only by --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob and --max-turns 40; its final message is treated as untrusted data by the CI steps that parse and redact it.

trustZones.name: AWS account (IAM role, STS, Amazon Bedrock)
trustZones.description: Maintainer-owned AWS account: the OIDC-federated IAM role for Bedrock, STS, and the Bedrock Runtime endpoints in vars.AWS_REGION. Trusted; exposure limited by the role's trust and permission policies (A009, A010).

trustZones.name: External vendors and package registries
trustZones.description: api.anthropic.com (fallback model provider), PyPI, npm/Bun registry, GitHub Releases for the Claude Code CLI, and the source repositories of the four third-party actions. Code and models fetched from here execute inside the runner with credentials present.

trustZones.name: CI unit-test job (runs PR code by design)
trustZones.description: The ci.yml job executes PR-authored tests and conftest.py for same-repo and fork PRs with contents:read only and no repository secrets. Deliberately low trust; attack 4 targets it.

trustZones.name: Demo asset service (hypothetical deployment)

crossingPoints.description: PR author pushes a branch and opens/updates a PR. GitHub authenticates the account; write access decides whether the resulting pull_request run receives secrets (same-repo) or not (fork). The content itself is never validated at this crossing.

Actions control plane schedules the job on a fresh runner, injects GITHUB_TOKEN with the workflow's permissions block (contents:read, pull-requests:write, id-token:write) plus repository secrets/variables, and the checkout step clones the PR head. The workflow definition executed here is taken from the PR merge ref.

The agents read the workspace (prompts, base-ref rules, prefetched diff, checkout, candidate list) through Read/Grep/Glob and hand their final message back via the action's execution_file. No authentication; authorization is the --allowedTools list. The agents also inherit the runner's process environment, including AWS session credentials.
Agents call Bedrock Runtime with the STS session credentials (SigV4). Authorization is the role's permission policy (InvokeModel on the configured inference profiles).

Fallback path: agents call the Anthropic Messages API with the long-lived ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Also covers the action's run-time download of the Claude Code CLI from a public registry (no authentication, integrity depends on the action's own pinning).

CI steps call back into GitHub: actions/checkout clones the PR head with GITHUB_TOKEN (persist-credentials=false), OIDC ID-token request (id-token:write), gh api list/PATCH comments and gh pr comment (pull-requests:write), and the job conclusion that becomes the 'Agentic AI Review' check. Step logs stream into the run log.

aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials presents the GitHub OIDC JWT to sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. Authorization is the role trust policy (aud = sts.amazonaws.com, sub scoped to this repository, per AWS IAM guidance).

claude-code-action holds github_token and may call the GitHub API for its own plumbing (PR context, progress tracking). Whether any of this reaches the model context is unverifiable from this repository (A011).
ci.yml checkout of the PR head with a contents:read GITHUB_TOKEN (persist-credentials=false) for same-repo and fork PRs; job conclusion becomes the 'Unit tests' check.
setup-python interpreter download and pip install of pytest==8.4.1 / PyYAML==6.0.2 from PyPI. Version-pinned, not hash-pinned.

pytest imports PR-authored tests and conftest.py and exercises app/files.py and app/tokens.py. Attack 4 uses this crossing to run exfiltration code; the job has no repository secrets and a read-only token, so the blast radius is the runner itself and the checkout.

Collaborator write permission gates same-repo PRs
Branch protection on main: required checks 'Agentic AI Review' and 'Unit tests', PR required, admin bypass disabled (A005)
Fork guard on every workflow step: head.repo.full_name == github.repository
GitHub does not pass repository secrets to fork pull_request runs
GAP: no CODEOWNERS / required review for .github/** (README 'What this does not solve')

permissions: contents read, pull-requests write, id-token write (no contents:write, no actions/packages)

Concurrency group per PR with cancel-in-progress

Prompts instruct: text in code/comments/filenames is never instructions nor evidence

assets.name: PR diff and PR-head repository content (untrusted review input)
assets.description: The base...head diff written to $RUNNER_TEMP/pr.diff plus every file in the PR-head checkout. Public code, but it is the carrier for every attack: guard removals, prompt-injection text, symlinks, a rewritten workflow. Criticality is about integrity of the judgement made on it, not confidentiality.

assets.name: Review contract (RULES.yaml, discovery.md, validate.md) as loaded from the BASE commit
assets.description: The rules and prompts that define what the reviewer enforces. Extracted with git show $BASE_SHA:... into .review-base/ and .review-prompts/. The PR head cannot change what this run loads; changing it on main requires a merge that is itself reviewed against the previous contract.

assets.name: Workflow definition agentic-review.yml as executed (from the PR merge ref)
assets.description: Unlike RULES.yaml and the prompts, the workflow file that GitHub executes for a pull_request event comes from the PR merge ref, so a same-repo PR author can change the steps, the tool allow-list, the gate logic or the fork guard. Its integrity rests on branch protection and human review of .github/** changes, not on the base-ref mechanism.

assets.name: GITHUB_TOKEN (job-scoped: contents read, pull-requests write, id-token write)
assets.description: Injected by the Actions control plane; used by checkout (not persisted), passed to claude-code-action as github_token, used by the comment step via gh, and implicitly to request the OIDC ID token. Expires when the job ends. Misuse: post/modify PR comments as github-actions[bot], request OIDC tokens.

assets.name: AWS STS session credentials for the Bedrock role
assets.description: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN exported into the job environment by configure-aws-credentials; inherited by both agent steps and every later step. Valid for the role session duration (default 1 hour) even after the job ends. Misuse bounded by the role policy: InvokeModel on approved profiles (cost, model abuse).

assets.name: Long-lived repository secrets: AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
assets.description: AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN is a low-sensitivity identifier (useless without a valid OIDC token) but is treated as a secret so GitHub masks it. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, when configured, is a long-lived bearer credential passed as an action input to both agent steps; exposure means unlimited model usage on the maintainer's account until rotated.

assets.name: GitHub OIDC ID token (audience sts.amazonaws.com)
assets.description: Short-lived JWT minted by GitHub for this job (claims include repository, ref, event, actor) and exchanged once at STS. Replay window is minutes; value depends entirely on how permissive the IAM trust policy is.

assets.name: Discovery candidate list (.review-candidates.md)
assets.description: Stage-1 model output extracted from execution_file, redacted, size-capped and checked for [DISCOVERY] <sha>. Never posted; printed to the run log. Treated by validate.md as UNTRUSTED EVIDENCE because it is model output derived from attacker text.

assets.name: Validation verdict (review-output.md) and SHA-scoped markers
assets.description: Stage-2 model output. The gate's decision is a pure function of this text: [REVIEWED] <head sha> must be present, [BLOCK-MERGE] <head sha> must be absent. Posted (redacted) as the PR comment. Forging or suppressing markers is the direct route to a false pass.

assets.name: 'Agentic AI Review' check-run conclusion on the PR head SHA
assets.description: The job exit code as recorded by GitHub. Branch protection consumes it. It is the only artifact that actually blocks or allows a merge; everything else is evidence.

assets.name: Run logs and execution transcripts
assets.description: Step output including cat of the redacted candidates and verdict, gh/jq stderr, and the action's own transcript output. Public on a public repository. Any redaction miss becomes a public disclosure harvested by bots (TA015).

assets.name: Demo asset service API token and asset-root files
assets.description: The expected token compared by verify_token and the files reachable through resolve_asset. Hypothetical in this sample; represents what a merged guard removal would expose in a real deployment (README bypass: img/../../secret.txt).

flows.description: Author pushes branch content and opens/updates the PR. Identity is authenticated and write-authorised; content is not validated.
actions/checkout clones the PR head (fetch-depth 0); git diff base...head is written to $RUNNER_TEMP/pr.diff. Only check: the diff must be non-empty.

Discovery agent reads the prefetched diff and any repository file with Read/Grep/Glob. This is where attacker text meets the model; the only defence is the prompt's instruction to treat in-code text as neither instruction nor evidence.
Validation agent independently re-reads the diff and repository files to falsify candidates.
Diff and read file content travel to Bedrock inside the model prompt. Public code; Bedrock does not store or share prompts.
ci.yml checks out and executes PR-authored tests/conftest.py. The job has a read-only token and no secrets, so attack 4 can only exfiltrate what is on that runner.
CONTROL 1: git show $BASE_SHA:RULES.yaml and both prompts into freshly recreated scratch dirs; the job exits 1 if a prompt is missing or empty on base.
Agents read .review-prompts/discovery.md or validate.md and .review-base/RULES.yaml. The invoking prompt says the file is the complete instruction set.
Validation agent reads validate.md and the base-ref RULES.yaml (authoritative blocking flags).
For pull_request events GitHub loads agentic-review.yml from the PR merge ref, so the PR author controls the steps that will run. No base-ref protection applies to the workflow file itself.
Runner executes the loaded workflow definition with the declared permissions and secrets.
Job-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN injected with contents:read, pull-requests:write, id-token:write.
checkout uses the token for the clone; persist-credentials=false prevents it from being written to .git/config where the agent could Read it.
github_token passed as an input to claude-code-action in both passes. Lives in the action's process environment next to the model-driven agent.
github_token passed to the validation pass.
GH_TOKEN used by gh api / gh pr comment to find, patch or create the single bot comment.
ci.yml's separate GITHUB_TOKEN is contents:read only; it is the only credential present while PR test code runs.
configure-aws-credentials requests the OIDC ID token from the Actions issuer using ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN (requires id-token: write).
sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity presents the JWT; STS validates signature, aud and the trust policy's sub condition (A009).
STS returns session credentials; the action exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/AWS_SESSION_TOKEN into the job environment for all later steps. GitHub masks the values in logs.

Discovery agent inherits the AWS session credentials from the environment (needed to sign Bedrock calls). The Read tool can also open /proc/self/environ or any file on the runner, so a prompt-injected agent can quote them into its output.
Validation agent inherits the same session credentials.
Credentials are used only to SigV4-sign Bedrock Runtime requests.

Repository secrets and variables injected into the same-repo run: AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN feeds the USE_BEDROCK presence test and role-to-assume; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (if set) feeds the anthropic_api_key input.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY passed as action input to both agent steps even when Bedrock is in use (empty string when unset). Long-lived; exposure requires rotation.
Fallback model calls authenticate to api.anthropic.com with the static key.

Capture step reads the discovery execution_file with jq, writes .review-candidates.md, perl-redacts credential shapes, fails closed if [DISCOVERY] <sha> is missing or size > 120000 bytes, then cats it to the log.
Validation agent reads the candidate list, instructed to treat it as UNTRUSTED EVIDENCE and to re-derive every finding from code.
Redacted candidate list printed to the public run log ('never posted' as a comment, but logged).
Capture step extracts the validation result from execution_file, redacts it into review-output.md; the gate then greps for [REVIEWED] <sha> and [BLOCK-MERGE] <sha>.
Comment step builds /tmp/review-comment.md (marker, heading, verdict line, model output) and posts/updates the github-actions[bot] comment on the PR.
Redacted verdict printed to the public run log.
Gate step exit code (1 on any abnormal path or [BLOCK-MERGE]) becomes the job conclusion.

Check run 'Agentic AI Review' recorded on the head SHA; branch protection reads it to allow or block the merge (A005). On fork PRs the job name differs and every step is skipped, so the required check never turns green.
All step output and the action's transcript are persisted as run logs, readable by anyone with repository read access.

resolve_asset()/read_asset() open files under asset_root after rejecting empty/padded/absolute paths and any resolved path outside the resolved root; verify_token() gates access with a constant-time compare and logs only a redacted token.

residualRiskAssessments.rationale: Code-only tools, no PR prose in context, base-ref prompts, two independent passes and SHA-scoped markers make a successful injection much harder, but the verdict is still model output read from attacker text. Impact is unchanged (vulnerable code merges). Stays open pending empirical measurement after every model/prompt change (M056) and Read path restrictions (M051).

The rules name the exact weak replacements and the validation pass must ground each finding in code, yet detection of a well-disguised three-line change is probabilistic. The README itself says the design is not a proof and must be measured; no measurement results ship with this checkout.

Nothing in the repository prevents a same-repo PR from rewriting agentic-review.yml, and GitHub runs the PR's version for pull_request events. The rules-may-only-tighten rule is enforced by the file being attacked. This is the top residual risk; it needs CODEOWNERS plus a code-owner-review ruleset (M046) now and a default-branch workflow_run lane (M047) for a durable fix.

The PR under review cannot alter what it is reviewed against (git show from BASE_SHA, exit 1 on a missing prompt), and weakening the contract is a blocking rule whose flag the validation prompt treats as authoritative. A disarming diff to RULES.yaml is also conspicuous. Remaining exposure runs through T003 (workflow edit), which is tracked separately.

Branch protection cannot be expressed or verified in the checkout, the README no longer documents it, and the check was renamed this session so an existing rule may still reference 'Hardened AI Review'. Until a ruleset requires 'Agentic AI Review' and 'Unit tests' with no bypass actors (M048), the gate is advisory.

The agent has no network or execution tool, so exfiltration needs a successful injection (T001) plus the CI comment/log channel; the checkout token is not persisted. But the redaction misses raw secret keys, session tokens and ghs_/sk-ant- prefixes, the API key is passed even when Bedrock is used, and Read can open /proc and $RUNNER_TEMP. M051, M052 and M049 (short sessions) are all low-cost.

All actions are SHA-pinned and test dependencies version-pinned, which removes the tag-mutation vector. The Claude Code CLI is still downloaded at run time inside the action after AWS credentials exist, and pip is not hash-pinned. Low likelihood, high impact; close with M054.

--allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob" in both passes gives the agent nothing that executes; the README reports the tool denial as visible in transcripts. The only route to re-enable it is editing the workflow, which is T003.

Running PR-authored tests is the purpose of ci.yml. The job holds only a contents:read token that is not persisted and no repository secrets, so the blast radius is public code. Accepted on condition that no secrets are ever added to the test job's environment.

Using OIDC instead of static keys is the right pattern, but the trust policy's aud/sub conditions live in AWS and were not verified. AWS documentation is explicit that an unscoped sub lets any repository assume the role. Open until the maintainer confirms the repository-scoped condition (M049).

Role permissions are outside the repository and unverified; the workflow also uses the default 1-hour session. Bounded impact if the policy is InvokeModel-only on the named profiles as the README instructs; open until confirmed and role-duration-seconds is shortened (M049).

Per-PR cost is bounded by the concurrency group, 30-minute timeout, 40-turn caps and the candidate-size cap, and the README explicitly accepts two model calls per PR as a cost of the design. Cross-PR abuse remains possible; an account-level budget alarm and draft-PR skip (M050) are recommended but not blocking for a demo repository.

Failing closed on vendor outages is the intended behaviour; the cost is a delayed merge and a manual re-run, which the posted comment already instructs. A bounded retry (M060) would reduce friction but must never convert a failure into a pass.

The validation prompt's falsification step, 80-point confidence floor and closed BLOCKING list are the available levers; residual false blocks are a property of using a model and the README says so. Track the rate alongside the attack corpus (M056) and define a code-owner override that does not weaken the check (M060).

Only a lower bound on diff size exists, so an attacker can dilute a small guard removal in a large or obfuscated diff and exhaust the agents' turns. A size ceiling and Trojan-Source character check in the prefetch step (M053) are a few lines of shell.
Every scratch path is removed before it is written, pr.diff lives outside the checkout, and no PR code runs in the review job before those writes. No further action.

The merge decision comes from the check run, not from comments, and the updater filters on the bot author plus marker. A look-alike comment can only mislead a human reader; adding run id/SHA to the marker and documenting the check run as authoritative (M057) is cheap hygiene.

Check-run annotations and run logs preserve the verdict for the log retention period; the comment is editable by design of GitHub. For a demo repository this is acceptable; upload artifacts (M055) if the pattern is reused where audit evidence matters.

The allow-list and the gate's reliance on the captured execution_file (not comments) contain the impact, but whether claude-code-action exposes any GitHub write path to the model despite --allowedTools was not inspected at the pinned SHA. Open until that is reviewed as part of the action-update process (M054).

Only the pull_request trigger is used, every step carries the fork guard, the job name differs on forks and GitHub withholds secrets from fork runs. This is a design constraint to preserve: any future fork lane must follow M047, never pull_request_target with a head checkout.

The repository is public and Apache-2.0; the diff and source carry no confidentiality requirement, and the primary Bedrock path does not store or share prompts per AWS documentation. Becomes relevant only if the pattern is reused on non-public code (M059).

Only a boolean is exposed and the credentials step's run/skip status reveals the same, so the risk is informational. Still open because the fix (move the env block under the job, M058) is trivial, was verified on copies this session, and clears the ASH finding.

resolve_asset rejects empty, padded and absolute paths and requires the fully resolved candidate to be the root or under it, which defeats img/../../secret.txt and symlink escapes. The no-guard-removal rule exists to keep this true; residual risk is T002 (a false negative on a future weakening).

hmac.compare_digest removes the timing channel and describe_token limits logs to a 4-character prefix plus length; the semgrep hit on the format string is a false positive by design. The no-secret-logging rule guards against regression.

softwareProfile.description: GitHub Actions workflow triggered by pull_request events (opened/synchronize/reopened). Job steps: checkout (persist-credentials=false, fetch-depth 0) -> extract RULES.yaml and prompts from BASE sha into .review-base/.review-prompts (fail if missing) -> prefetch diff base...head into $RUNNER_TEMP/pr.diff (fail if empty) -> assume AWS role via OIDC (aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials, only if AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN set) -> Discovery pass (anthropics/claude-code-action, model DISCOVERY_MODEL default us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob, --max-turns 40) -> capture candidates from execution_file, redact, fail closed on missing [DISCOVERY] marker or >120000 bytes -> Validation pass (same action, model VALIDATION_MODEL default us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8) -> capture+redact review-output.md -> CI step posts/updates ONE PR comment keyed by hidden marker via gh api (GITHUB_TOKEN) -> gate step exits 1 unless [REVIEWED] <head sha> present and [BLOCK-MERGE] <head sha> absent. Every step is guarded by head.repo.full_name == github.repository (fork guard). Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. Permissions: contents read, pull-requests write, id-token write. Concurrency group per PR with cancel-in-progress. A separate ci.yml runs pytest. The demo app is a pure-Python library (no HTTP layer in this checkout).

dataAssetProfiles.name: Pull request diff and repository source code
dataAssetProfiles.description: Attacker-controllable input: the base...head diff prefetched to $RUNNER_TEMP/pr.diff plus the full checkout the agent may Read/Grep/Glob. Public Apache-2.0 code, so confidentiality is low; integrity of what the reviewer judges is what matters.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Review contract: RULES.yaml, review prompts, agentic-review.yml
dataAssetProfiles.description: Defines what the reviewer enforces and how the gate decides. Read from the BASE commit at runtime. Integrity-critical: weakening it is itself a blocking violation (rules-may-only-tighten). The workflow file itself is only protected by repository branch protection/CODEOWNERS, which this repo does not ship.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Workflow credentials: GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS OIDC role ARN and STS session credentials, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
dataAssetProfiles.description: GITHUB_TOKEN (contents:read, pull-requests:write, id-token:write) is handed to claude-code-action and the comment step; short-lived AWS credentials from aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials live in the job environment for the model-call steps; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is an optional fallback. Exposure enables PR-comment spoofing, model-invocation cost abuse, or Bedrock access within the role's policy.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Model outputs: discovery candidates, validation verdict, posted PR comment
dataAssetProfiles.description: .review-candidates.md (never posted), review-output.md (posted after regex redaction), and the SHA-scoped markers the gate parses. Integrity of the verdict is the whole point of the system; the comment is public on a public repo.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Workflow run logs and Claude execution transcripts
dataAssetProfiles.description: GitHub Actions logs (the workflow cats redacted candidates and review output) and the claude-code-action execution_file. Readable by anyone with read access to the repository; on a public repository that is everyone.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Demo asset service data: API token and files under the asset root
dataAssetProfiles.description: The review target's own data: the expected API token compared in app/tokens.py and the files served from asset_root in app/files.py. Not deployed anywhere in this sample; modelled because the attack PRs target these controls and the reviewer must catch their weakening.

userPersonas.name: Repository maintainer / demo presenter
threat_actor_overlay: Mistaken configuration (branch protection, OIDC trust policy, secrets)
userPersonas.description: Owns the GitHub repository, configures secrets (AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, DEMO_FAKE_SECRET), variables, branch protection and the IAM role trust policy. Can bypass the gate by design of GitHub if admin bypass is left enabled.

userPersonas.name: Same-repository contributor (write access)
userPersonas.description: Can push branches and open PRs that run agentic-review.yml WITH repository secrets. This is the adversary the four demo attack PRs model: smuggles guard removal, plants prompt injection in code comments and PR body, disarms RULES.yaml/prompts, adds conftest.py that exfiltrates CI secrets.

userPersonas.description: Any GitHub account can open a fork PR against a public repository. The workflow renders the check name but every step is skipped for fork PRs; secrets are not passed to fork-triggered pull_request runs. A fork PR still exercises ci.yml (pytest) without secrets.

userPersonas.name: GitHub Actions workflow identity (GITHUB_TOKEN)

userPersonas.name: AI reviewer agent (Claude Code via claude-code-action)
userPersonas.description: Two invocations (discovery, validation) with --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob and --max-turns 40, running on the runner with the AWS session credentials in its process environment and the prefetched diff plus full checkout on disk. Reads attacker-controlled text; modelled as potentially compromised (prompt injection) so its only output channel, the final message, is treated as untrusted by CI.

userPersonas.description: Receives the diff, any files the agent reads, and the prompts; returns the model output. Bedrock in vars.AWS_REGION (default us-west-2) via the OIDC-assumed role, or api.anthropic.com with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

userPersonas.name: Third-party GitHub Actions (checkout, setup-python, configure-aws-credentials, claude-code-action)
userPersonas.description: Code executed inside the job with access to GITHUB_TOKEN and, for claude-code-action, the AWS session credentials. All four are pinned to full commit SHAs with version comments. claude-code-action installs the Claude Code CLI at run time.

userPersonas.name: Public reader / demo audience
threat_actor_overlay: Passive observer of leaked data in logs/comments
userPersonas.description: Anyone can read the public repository, PR comments (including the posted review), and Actions logs (which contain the redacted candidate list and review output).

userPersonas.name: Asset service client (demo app)
userPersonas.description: Hypothetical caller of app.files.read_asset(asset_root, requested) and app.tokens.verify_token(presented, expected). Supplies the requested path and the presented token; modelled malicious because the demo PRs try to weaken exactly these two controls.

nonFunctionalRequirements.rationale: Core design property: missing prompt, empty diff, missing [DISCOVERY]/[REVIEWED] marker, oversized candidates, errored step, or [BLOCK-MERGE] all exit 1 and block the merge.
LLM verdicts are nondeterministic; two passes plus a closed blocking list raise the bar but the README asks for empirical measurement (10 runs per attack) rather than assuming correctness.
Depends on GitHub Actions, GitHub-hosted runners and Bedrock/Anthropic availability. Outages block merges (fail closed) rather than allowing them; acceptable for a demo repository.
Recovery is a workflow re-run; no persistent state beyond PR comments.
